idiom_name: block-taking accessor: owner.with { |r| ... }; the owner returns the resource in ensure
implementation_notes: Ruby's local idiom moves the hand-back to the owner: the lending method takes a block, hands the resource to it and returns the block's value - File.open's block form is the standard example ('with a block given, calls the block with the File object and returns the block's value') - releasing the resource in an ensure clause. The borrower never receives a release obligation, which is a stronger form of the pattern than handing out a wrapper; when a resource must escape the block the borrower has to hold it explicitly and a wrapper whose close hands back becomes justified, but that is the exception. Model the common case as a block-taking method on the pool or owner.
code_sketch:
pool.with_connection do |conn|       # owner yields, ensures the hand-back
  handle(conn)
end                                  # ensure => pool.checkin(conn)

def with_connection
  conn = checkout
  begin
    yield conn
  ensure
    checkin(conn)                    # hand back on any exit
  end
end
pitfalls: Returning the resource out of the block (or storing it in an instance variable) escapes the hand-back: the owner has already checked it in while the borrower still uses it.
ensure runs the hand-back even when the block raised; an exception raised inside ensure replaces the original one, so the check-in must not raise or the real failure is lost.
break/next/throw inside the block unwind through ensure, and the block's value is what the method returns - so a jump silently changes the caller's result; document the block contract.
